content.text:
I've started an agent that checks how portable each skill is: hardcoded paths, prerequisites, and what can be packaged as a Claude Code plugin. Questions that depend on its answers will come in round 2. Here's round 1:

❓ **Q1: Who exactly is the audience, and where can they see it?**
- (a) Only the DG engineering team (Michael, Sid, Johnny, maparent and others), private to the org.
- (b) The wider DG group, including researchers and designers who code a little.
- (c) Public, for anyone. Good for the open-source story, but every DG-specific detail (Roam dev graph, Linear, vault names) would need to be generalised or explained.

➡️ **(a) or (b), private to the DiscourseGraphs org.** Your description ("beginner, wants better vibe coding") sounds like (b). Keeping it private means you can leave DG specifics in, like Linear, the dev graph and the repo conventions, instead of making them generic.

---

❓ **Q2: Share now, or after more real use?** Since the build, you've used it on real tickets (your memory notes show vault leases, harness fixes and the pr-evidence image problem). Options:
- (a) Share now, with each piece labelled *proven*, *works with caveats* or *experimental*.
- (b) Wait until the pilot tally is written up.

➡️ **(a).** Labels are honest and let people pick the safe parts first. The tally can come later as a short "what I learned" note.

---

❓ **Q3: Where do the skills live, so teammates can install them?**
- (a) **A new GitHub repo set up as a Claude Code plugin marketplace.** Teammates run `/plugin marketplace add DiscourseGraphs/<repo>` and `/plugin install <name>`. That's one command per module, no file copying, and updates arrive with `/plugin update`.
- (b) **The existing monorepo's `.agents/skills`.** The team already shares skills there, so everyone gets them on `git pull`. But that makes it a team convention through a PR, and Codex users get them too.
- (c) **A plain repo of folders** with copy-paste install steps.
- (d) **A Claude artifact only**, with links to the files.

➡️ **(a), with an artifact or README as the friendly front door.** For beginners, "run this one command" beats "copy these folders and symlink them." A plugin keeps your personal workflow separate from team conventions, which fits personal-first. Items that are already team skills (scope-check, adherence check, writing style) stay in the monorepo and the plugin just links to them. An artifact on its own can't install anything.

---

❓ **Q4: All-or-nothing, or modules people pick from?** You said parts or all. Proposed split, ordered from easiest to adopt to most setup:

| Module | What you get | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Ideas only | Plan first, prove it with evidence, two human gates. No install. | none |
| 1. Plan and checkpoint | `/start`, `/checkpoint` with an Approved plan section | Obsidian vault path |
| 2. PR autopilot | `/create-pr`, `babysit`, `pr-queue` sweep | gh CLI |
| 3. Evidence | `pr-evidence` (screenshots to Roam) | Roam Playwright slot |
| 4. Obsidian live verification | `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`, `obsidian-vault` | test vaults |

➡️ **Modules, each a separate installable plugin**, with a "requires" line where one depends on another. For example, create-pr is better with evidence but works without it. Module 0 is the most valuable part for beginners.

---

❓ **Q5: Codex users?** Some teammates use Codex. The team skills in `.agents/skills` already ship Codex metadata (`openai.yaml`). Options:
- (a) Claude Code only.
- (b) Claude Code first, with a note on which modules work in Codex.
- (c) Both, fully supported.

➡️ **(b).** Several pieces rely on Claude-Code-only features (subagents, the PR monitor, push notifications). Full Codex support would double the work for an audience that's just getting started.

---

❓ **Q6: What's the front door?** Wherever the files live, someone with no context needs one page to read first. Options:
- (a) **The repo README.** GitHub draws Mermaid diagrams natively, so the diagram renders there. It sits right next to the install commands.
- (b) **A Claude artifact.** Nicer design, plus your Roam screenshot, but it lives apart from the files.
- (c) **Both.** The README is the source of truth, and the artifact is a polished tour that links to it.

➡️ **(a), with the PNG diagram embedded as a fallback.** One place to read and install keeps it simple for beginners. Your existing artifact can become (c) later if you want something to present.

content.text:
**Q3: what a plugin marketplace needs, and how A differs from C**

It isn't hard. Both options start from the same folder of skills and commands. A adds two small JSON files, plus one real job: rewriting script paths.

```
dg-workflow/                          ← GitHub repo
  .claude-plugin/marketplace.json     ← A only: "this repo offers plugin X" (~10 lines)
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json          ← A only: name, version, description (~10 lines)
  skills/create-pr/SKILL.md …         ← same in A and C
  commands/start.md …                 ← same in A and C
  hooks/hooks.json                    ← A only: e.g. the pr-receipts gate
  README.md
```

| | **A: plugin marketplace** | **C: plain repo** |
|---|---|---|
| Teammate installs | `/plugin marketplace add DiscourseGraphs/dg-workflow`, then `/plugin install dg-workflow` | Clone it, then copy or symlink folders into `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.claude/commands` |
| Updates | `/plugin marketplace update` | `git pull`, then copy again |
| Hooks (e.g. the PR receipts gate) | Ship inside the plugin | Each person edits their own `settings.json` by hand |
| Command names | Prefixed with the plugin name: `/dg-workflow:create-pr` | Unchanged: `/create-pr` |
| Extra work for you | The two JSON files, and changing every `~/.claude/skills/...` path in scripts to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...` | None |
| Where beginners trip | Rarely | Wrong folders, broken symlinks, a forgotten hook |

A private org repo should work, since installing uses the teammate's own GitHub access. I'll confirm that with a real install when we build it.

**Settled so far:**
- **Audience and status:** private to the DG org, shared now with *proven / caveats / experimental* labels.
- **Packaging:** a plugin repo, as one plugin with a setup step, since people can just ignore commands they don't want.
- **Supporting pieces:** Claude Code first, with Codex notes. The front door is a **Claude artifact**.
- **Docs and dependencies:** checkpoint gets a one-line "why" and a one-line "what". Setup tells people to install the outside plugins you rely on: mattpocock-skills (`grill-me`, `grilling`, `teach`, `handoff`, `tdd`…) and others.

---

## Round 2

❓ **Q7: Repo and plugin name.** The plugin name becomes the prefix on every command, so a short one is easier to type.
- (a) `dg-workflow`, so commands look like `/dg-workflow:start`
- (b) `dgflow`, so `/dgflow:start`
- (c) something else

➡️ **(b) `dgflow`, in the private repo `DiscourseGraphs/dgflow`.** Short to type, and still clearly DG's.

---

❓ **Q8: What `/dgflow:setup` does.** Proposal, as one guided conversation:
1. **Check prerequisites:** `gh auth status`, whether Linear is connected, pnpm, Node version. It explains how to fix anything missing.
2. **Ask for personal values:**
   - where to keep checkpoints
   - where their discourse-graph checkout lives
   - which Roam slot uploads screenshots, and which Roam page holds them (default `<Name> test/`)
   - their Obsidian test vaults, and which vault is production and must never be used
3. **Save the answers** to `~/.claude/dgflow.env`. Every script reads that file instead of hardcoded paths.
4. **Print the install commands** for the outside plugins. A plugin can't install other plugins, so the person pastes these.
5. **Optional, macOS only:** set up the 30-minute background PR sweep.

➡️ **Accept.** It's the one place beginners make choices, and re-running it is how they change their mind later.

---

❓ **Q9: Default checkpoint storage for people who don't use Obsidian.** Checkpoints are plain markdown files.
- (a) Require an Obsidian vault.
- (b) Default to a plain folder like `~/dgflow-sessions/`. Obsidian users can point it at a vault folder instead.

➡️ **(b).** It works for everyone, and Obsidian users still get your setup.

The two one-liners for the artifact:
- *Why:* "Agent sessions forget everything when they end. A checkpoint saves the reasoning so the next session, or a teammate, picks up where you left off."
- *What:* "Writes the goal, decisions, approved plan and next step for this branch into one markdown file."

---

❓ **Q10: What ships in the plugin?** Proposed:

| Ship | Leave out |
|---|---|
| `start`, `go-ticket`, `cleanup-ticket`, `checkpoint`, `create-pr`, `babysit`, `pr-queue` with the sweep scripts, the `pr-receipts` hook, `pr-evidence`, `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`, `obsidian-vault`, `explain-diff-html` | `aiday` (personal), `roam-switch` (tied to your `~/roam-ext-dev` setup), `obsidian-release` (a release chore, and a team skill already exists) |

Your name and reviewer names ("Trang approved…", "mdroidian") in the skill text get replaced with generic wording or values from config.

➡️ **Accept.** Should `roam-switch` ship anyway, with its path coming from config? Your call. I'd leave it out unless teammates also develop the Roam extension in several worktrees.

---

❓ **Q11: Do you switch to the plugin yourself?** Once it exists, you'd have two copies, the plugin and `~/.claude`, and they would drift apart. Your own CLAUDE.md rule warns about exactly that.
- (a) You switch to the plugin and delete the personal copies, backed up first. Your commands get the `dgflow:` prefix too.
- (b) Keep your personal copies and sync the plugin by hand.

➡️ **(a).** One source of truth, and you'll hit the same rough edges your teammates do.

---

❓ **Q12: The artifact's structure (your Q6 choice).** For a beginner reader, top to bottom:
1. **The problem, in one paragraph:** "agents write code fast; the hard part is trusting it."
2. **The diagram, redrawn in plain language.** Boxes say what happens ("Agent tests it in the real app"), with the command shown as a small tag underneath, and a legend: you / agent / both.
3. **Pick what you want:** one card per piece, each with a one-line "what", a one-line "why", a proven / caveats / experimental badge, and what it needs.
4. **Install:** three copy-button steps (add the marketplace, install, run setup), plus the outside plugins.
5. **A glossary** of words the reader may not know: worktree, CI, PR template, bot review, CDP, scenario.
6. **Your real Roam screenshot**, as an example of evidence.

The repo's README is just a short pointer to the artifact plus the install commands.

➡️ **Accept.** The glossary matters most for this audience, and putting the plain-language words first and commands second is what makes the diagram readable without context.

content.text:
Settled: `roam-switch` ships, with its path taken from config, and all my other recommendations stand.

**Q11: how maintenance differs**

| | **(a) Switch fully to the plugin** | **(b) Two copies, synced by hand** | **(c) Plugin is the stable version, personal folder is your lab** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where you experiment | Branches in the `dgflow` repo | Your `~/.claude` copies | `~/.claude/skills`, as before |
| What teammates get | Whatever lands on `main` | Whatever you remember to copy over | Only what you deliberately graduate by PR |
| Drift risk | None, one copy | High: every fix gets made twice, or forgotten | Low, if experiments stay short-lived |
| Overhead per experiment | Make a branch, switch your install to it, switch back | Copying files around | None. Edit and try it. |
| Weakness | Clumsy for quick "let me try X" changes | The drift your own CLAUDE.md warns about | A forked skill can quietly turn into a permanent second copy |

One fact makes (c) clean: plugin commands carry a prefix and personal ones don't, so `/dgflow:create-pr` and your own `/create-pr` can exist side by side without conflict. You can fork a team skill into your lab, try changes on your own tickets, and teammates never see them.

❓ **Q11 (restated):**

➡️ **(c), with three rules:**
1. **Install the plugin from GitHub like everyone else**, so you see exactly what teammates see.
2. **New ideas start in `~/.claude/skills`.** Once an idea has proved itself on two or three tickets, graduate it with a PR to `dgflow` and delete your personal copy.
3. **If you fork a plugin skill, note it in your checkpoint** with the date you expect to graduate or drop the fork. That keeps forks from becoming permanent.

---

These two follow from Q11 and are the last branches:

❓ **Q13: How teammates learn what changed.**
- (a) Keep a version in `plugin.json` plus a short `CHANGELOG.md`, each entry tagged proven / caveats / experimental, and post a one-line Slack note on notable releases.
- (b) Changelog only, no announcements.
- (c) Nothing formal.

➡️ **(a).** Beginners won't read commits. A one-line changelog entry plus a Slack note is how they find out `/dgflow:create-pr` got better.

---

❓ **Q14: How teammates give feedback and contribute.**
- (a) GitHub issues on the `dgflow` repo for problems and ideas, and PRs welcome, with you as the reviewer. `/dgflow:setup` prints the issues link.
- (b) Feedback in Slack only; you make all the changes.
- (c) Both: Slack for quick questions, issues for anything you'll act on.

➡️ **(c).** Slack is easier for beginners to ask in. Issues make sure feedback doesn't get lost. You stay the only reviewer for now.

Once you answer Q11, Q13 and Q14, every branch is settled. I'll then summarise the full design for your confirmation, then write the build plan, then build.

content.text:
That settles the last branch. Here's the full design to confirm before I write the build plan.

## dgflow: team handoff design

**Audience and status**
- DG team members who know GitHub but are beginner programmers and want to vibe-code better.
- Private to the DiscourseGraphs org. Shared now, with every piece labelled *proven*, *caveats* or *experimental*.
- Claude Code first, with notes on which pieces also work in Codex.

**Front door: a Claude artifact**, shared with the org, in this order:
1. The problem, in one paragraph: agents write code fast; the hard part is trusting it.
2. The diagram redrawn in plain language, with each command as a small tag and a you / agent / both legend.
3. One card per piece: what it does, why it helps, its badge, what it needs. Checkpoint gets the why and what lines we agreed.
4. Install in three copy-button steps, plus the outside plugins (mattpocock-skills: `grill-me`, `grilling`, `teach`, `handoff`, `tdd`…).
5. A glossary: worktree, CI, PR template, bot review, CDP, scenario.
6. Your real Roam screenshot as an example of evidence.

**Files: a private repo `DiscourseGraphs/dgflow`**, set up as a Claude Code plugin marketplace with one plugin, `dgflow`.
- **Install:** `/plugin marketplace add DiscourseGraphs/dgflow`, then `/plugin install dgflow`, then `/dgflow:setup`.
- **Ships:**
  - commands and skills: `start`, `go-ticket`, `cleanup-ticket`, `roam-switch`, `checkpoint`, `create-pr`, `babysit`, `pr-queue` with the sweep scripts, `pr-evidence`, `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`, `obsidian-vault`, `explain-diff-html`
  - the `pr-receipts` hook
- **Left out:** `aiday` and `obsidian-release`.
- **Prerequisites:** team skills already in the monorepo (scope-check, adherence check, writing style, delegated review) are listed, not copied.
- **README:** a short pointer to the artifact, plus the install commands.

**`/dgflow:setup`**
1. Checks prerequisites (gh, Linear, pnpm, Node) and explains how to fix anything missing.
2. Asks for personal values: checkpoint folder (default `~/dgflow-sessions/`; Obsidian users can point it at a vault), repo checkout path, Roam slot and page (default `<Name> test/`), Obsidian test vaults and which one is production.
3. Saves the answers to `~/.claude/dgflow.env`. All scripts read it; no hardcoded paths stay.
4. Prints the install commands for the outside plugins, plus where to ask questions and report problems.
5. Optional, macOS only: sets up the background PR sweep.

**Generalising**
- Your name and reviewer names come out of the skill text.
- Script paths switch to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.

**Maintenance**
- The plugin is the stable version. You install it from GitHub like everyone else.
- Experiments live in your personal `~/.claude/skills`, with no prefix. An experiment that proves itself on two or three tickets graduates into `dgflow`, and your copy gets deleted.
- If you fork a plugin skill, note it in your checkpoint with the date you expect to graduate or drop it.
- `plugin.json` carries a version, and `CHANGELOG.md` gets tagged entries. Notable releases get a one-line Slack note.
- **Feedback:** anyone can commit directly to the repo. It's informal. Questions go to Slack.

Is this the shared understanding? If so, I'll write the build plan, with a verification step for each part:
- a real install from GitHub in a clean setup
- a `/dgflow:setup` dry run
- one command run end to end through the plugin

I'd also checkpoint this design before building.

mkdir -p ~/Desktop/code/dgflow && cd ~/Desktop/code/dgflow && git init -q -b main && mkdir -p .claude-plugin skills commands hooks scripts/lib && cat > CONFIG.md <<'EOF'
# dgflow config contract

Every script and skill reads personal values from `~/.claude/dgflow.env` (written by `/dgflow:setup`).
Precedence: an exported env var wins over the file, and the file wins over the default below. Never hardcode these values.

| Key | Default | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `DGFLOW_SESSIONS_DIR` | `~/dgflow-sessions` | checkpoint, start, go-ticket (session-context.sh) |
| `DGFLOW_REPO_DIR` | `~/Desktop/code/discourse-graph` | start, roam-switch, cleanup-ticket |
| `DGFLOW_GITHUB_REPO` | `DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph` | create-pr, babysit |
| `DGFLOW_WORKTREES_DIR` | `$DGFLOW_REPO_DIR/.claude/worktrees` | start, go-ticket, cleanup-ticket |
| `DGFLOW_ROAM_SLOT` | `1` | pr-evidence |
| `DGFLOW_ROAM_EVIDENCE_PAGE` | `dgflow evidence/` | pr-evidence |
| `DGFLOW_ROAM_EXT_DEV_LINK` | `~/roam-ext-dev` | roam-switch, start |
| `DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_APP` | `/Applications/Obsidian.app` | dg-obsidian-cdp-verify |
| `DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_CDP_PORT` | `9222` | dg-obsidian-cdp-verify |
| `DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_VAULTS` | (empty) | comma-separated absolute vault ROOT paths; obsidian-vault, dg-obsidian-cdp-verify |
| `DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_PRODUCTION_VAULT` | (empty) | vault root that is never leased or written to |
| `DGFLOW_REVIEW_BOTS` | `devin-ai-integration,chatgpt-codex-connector,graphite-app` | create-pr, babysit |
| `DGFLOW_STATE_DIR` | `~/.claude/state/dgflow` | obsidian-vault registry, misc state |

Loaders: `scripts/lib/config.sh` (`source` it; exports every key with defaults applied) and `scripts/lib/config.mjs` (`import { config } from ...`; returns an object keyed by the same names, `~` expanded).

Inside skills and commands, reference plugin files as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/...` or `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<name>/...`. Never `~/.claude/skills/...`.
EOF
cat > scripts/lib/config.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Source me. Env vars win over ~/.claude/dgflow.env, which wins over defaults (see CONFIG.md).
_dgflow_file="${DGFLOW_CONFIG:-$HOME/.claude/dgflow.env}"
if [ -f "$_dgflow_file" ]; then
  while IFS='=' read -r _k _v; do
    case "$_k" in DGFLOW_*) [ -z "${!_k+x}" ] && export "$_k=$(eval echo "$_v")" ;; esac
  done < <(grep -E '^DGFLOW_[A-Z_]+=' "$_dgflow_file")
fi
: "${DGFLOW_SESSIONS_DIR:=$HOME/dgflow-sessions}"
: "${DGFLOW_REPO_DIR:=$HOME/Desktop/code/discourse-graph}"
: "${DGFLOW_GITHUB_REPO:=DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph}"
: "${DGFLOW_WORKTREES_DIR:=$DGFLOW_REPO_DIR/.claude/worktrees}"
: "${DGFLOW_ROAM_SLOT:=1}"
: "${DGFLOW_ROAM_EVIDENCE_PAGE:=dgflow evidence/}"
: "${DGFLOW_ROAM_EXT_DEV_LINK:=$HOME/roam-ext-dev}"
: "${DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_APP:=/Applications/Obsidian.app}"
: "${DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_CDP_PORT:=9222}"
: "${DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_VAULTS:=}"
: "${DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_PRODUCTION_VAULT:=}"
: "${DGFLOW_REVIEW_BOTS:=devin-ai-integration,chatgpt-codex-connector,graphite-app}"
: "${DGFLOW_STATE_DIR:=$HOME/.claude/state/dgflow}"
export DGFLOW_SESSIONS_DIR DGFLOW_REPO_DIR DGFLOW_GITHUB_REPO DGFLOW_WORKTREES_DIR DGFLOW_ROAM_SLOT \
  DGFLOW_ROAM_EVIDENCE_PAGE DGFLOW_ROAM_EXT_DEV_LINK DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_APP DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_CDP_PORT \
  DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_VAULTS DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_PRODUCTION_VAULT DGFLOW_REVIEW_BOTS DGFLOW_STATE_DIR
unset _dgflow_file _k _v
EOF
cat > scripts/lib/config.mjs <<'EOF'
import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { homedir } from "node:os";

const HOME = homedir();
const expand = (v) => v.replace(/^~(?=\/|$)/, HOME).replace(/\$HOME|\$\{HOME\}/g, HOME);

const readFile = () => {
  const file = process.env.DGFLOW_CONFIG ?? `${HOME}/.claude/dgflow.env`;
  if (!existsSync(file)) return {};
  return Object.fromEntries(
    readFileSync(file, "utf8")
      .split("\n")
      .map((l) => l.match(/^(DGFLOW_[A-Z_]+)=(.*)$/))
      .filter(Boolean)
      .map(([, k, v]) => [k, v.trim().replace(/^(['"])(.*)\1$/, "$2")]),
  );
};

const fromFile = readFile();
const get = (k, fallback) => expand(process.env[k] ?? fromFile[k] ?? fallback);

const repoDir = get("DGFLOW_REPO_DIR", "~/Desktop/code/discourse-graph");

// Keys and defaults mirror CONFIG.md and config.sh.
export const config = {
  DGFLOW_SESSIONS_DIR: get("DGFLOW_SESSIONS_DIR", "~/dgflow-sessions"),
  DGFLOW_REPO_DIR: repoDir,
  DGFLOW_GITHUB_REPO: get("DGFLOW_GITHUB_REPO", "DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph"),
  DGFLOW_WORKTREES_DIR: get("DGFLOW_WORKTREES_DIR", `${repoDir}/.claude/worktrees`),
  DGFLOW_ROAM_SLOT: get("DGFLOW_ROAM_SLOT", "1"),
  DGFLOW_ROAM_EVIDENCE_PAGE: get("DGFLOW_ROAM_EVIDENCE_PAGE", "dgflow evidence/"),
  DGFLOW_ROAM_EXT_DEV_LINK: get("DGFLOW_ROAM_EXT_DEV_LINK", "~/roam-ext-dev"),
  DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_APP: get("DGFLOW_OBSIDIAN_APP", "/Applications/Obsidian.app"),

content.content:
## Install

In Claude Code, run these one at a time. The first line is usually already set up; running it again is harmless.

```bash
/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official
```

```bash
/plugin marketplace add DiscourseGraphs/dgflow
```

```bash
/plugin install dgflow@dgflow
```

```bash
/dgflow:setup
```

Installing dgflow also installs `mattpocock-skills` (planning and teaching skills the flow uses), which is why the first line is needed. If `/plugin list` says dgflow "failed to load" because of a missing dependency, run the first line and install again.

Setup checks your tools, asks for your personal settings, and writes `~/.claude/dgflow.env`. See [CONFIG.md](CONFIG.md) for every setting.

content.text:
dgflow is built and pushed, and the guide page is published.

**What teammates get**
- **The guide (start here):** **[dgflow: get from ticket to a PR you can trust](https://claude.ai/artifact/VBPuxtqqo6TRW8CkMdyZgx)**. It covers:
  - why dgflow exists
  - the flow diagram, with your verification branches added, plus the same flow as six plain steps
  - "pick what you need" shortcuts
  - a card for each of the 12 commands, with a status badge and a link to its file
  - copyable install steps
  - the companion skills and a glossary
  - your Roam screenshot as an example of the proof
- **The repo:** [DiscourseGraphs/dgflow](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/dgflow), private. Installing takes four lines in Claude Code, and setup then asks each person for their own folders, Roam slot and vaults.

**Verified**
- Passes Claude Code's strict plugin validator.
- A clean install straight from the private GitHub repo works, and pulls in mattpocock-skills automatically.
- Scripts run correctly from the installed copy, and a scan for your name, paths and vault names finds nothing.
- **Not yet tested:** `/dgflow:setup` run interactively from start to finish. Running it yourself once would be a good first test.

**Things that came up**
- **Install order matters.** The automatic mattpocock-skills install only works if Anthropic's official plugin marketplace is already added. Otherwise dgflow fails to load. The README and the guide now have people add that marketplace first.
- **Team skills don't show up in fresh clones.** The discourse-graph repo doesn't commit its `.claude/skills` links, so a fresh clone can't see scope-check, the adherence check and the other team skills. Setup works around this, but the real fix belongs in the monorepo.
- **Lost scratch files.** The temporary folder was cleaned out mid-build, so the guide's source now lives in the repo at `docs/guide.html`.

**Needs you**
1. **Share the guide** with the org from its Share menu. It's private until you do.
2. **Switch your own setup to the plugin?** Per the plan, you'd install dgflow from GitHub and remove your personal copies of the 11 ported skills and commands, plus the duplicate PR-receipts hook entries in `~/.claude/settings.json`. Your experiments stay personal. I'll back everything up first. Say the word and I'll do it.
3. **Automatic session snapshot:** it's on for everyone by default. Keep it, or make it opt-in?

content.text:
I updated the guide and republished it at the same link: **[dgflow guide](https://claude.ai/artifact/VBPuxtqqo6TRW8CkMdyZgx)**. The source in the repo (`docs/guide.html`) is pushed too. I haven't opened the published page to check how the diagram renders.

**Diagram changes**
- **Orange now means "you run it or decide it"**:
  - start a ticket (`/dgflow:start`)
  - plan with the agent
  - approve the plan
  - save it (`/dgflow:checkpoint`)
  - the final review, Loom and review request
- **Purple** means the agent stops and asks you. **White** means it runs on its own. The legend under the diagram says the same.
- **Planning** now shows `/mattpocock-skills:grill-me` stress-testing the plan.
- **Checkpoint** is now a step you run: "You save the approved plan". You're right that it's a deliberate choice, not something the agent does on its own.
- **create-pr** stays white, with a note: "you run it if you didn't say 'ship when verified'".
- **The step list below the diagram** matches: planning mentions grill-me, there's a new "Save the plan" step, and create-pr says when you run it yourself.

**Bug fixed:** in the version you saw, the "babysit" box and the "Clicks through Roam" box had the same internal name, so Mermaid merged them into one box. They're separate now.

**Sharing:** the page is now set to **"Anyone with the link"**, which means people outside the org can open it too. It describes private team tooling and links the private repo. Outsiders couldn't install anything, but if you meant org-only, switch it back in the Share menu.

I fixed both and republished at the same link: **[dgflow guide](https://claude.ai/artifact/VBPuxtqqo6TRW8CkMdyZgx)**.

- **The diagram now shows.** The diagram itself had no errors (it rendered fine in a normal browser); the page viewer just doesn't draw Mermaid. So I rendered it to an image and embedded that. The image sits on a white card so it reads in dark mode too.
- **Table of contents at the top**, right under the intro: nine numbered links in two columns, which stack into one column on a phone. I removed the old side menu, which only appeared on wide screens.

I checked one local preview of the top of the page: the contents, the intro and the diagram's colors all look right. I made two small layout tweaks after that check (aligning the two columns and widening the diagram) and didn't re-check them.

To change the diagram later, edit `docs/flow.mmd` in the repo and re-render it to `docs/flow.png`. Or ask me and I'll do it. All of this is pushed to `DiscourseGraphs/dgflow`.

Still open from before: the page is shared as "Anyone with the link", whether to switch your own setup to the plugin, and whether the automatic session snapshot stays on by default.
